newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabian shares up 1.17 percent in week.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabian shares up 1.17 percent in week.

text.p: Saudi Arabian stocks ended 1.17 percent higher in moderate trade last week, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index closed at 152.83 points on Thursday from 151.07 points the previous week. Of the 57 companies traded, 42 rose, five fell and 10 were unchanged.

Services sector shares dominated trade, accounting for 34 percent of volume. BFA said turnover in the week was 3.5 million shares worth 642 million riyals ($171 million) from 3.24 million shares worth 666 million riyals the previous week.

The biggest gainer was Saudi Industrial Development Company, which closed almost 12 percent higher at 85 riyals. It was one of the most active stocks, accounting for 11.4 percent of volume traded, BFA figures show.
Another active stock was Saudi Basic Industries Corp, which accounted for 13.4 percent of value traded. It ended three riyals up at 401 riyals.

United Saudi Commercial Bank gained good ground in the week, adding almost nine percent to 333 riyals. Al-Baha was another climber, ending four riyals firmer at 60. Aseer gathered three riyals to end at 66 riyals.
After notching up five riyals the previous week, Tabuk Agricultural Development Co was the biggest loser last week. It slid 3.3 percent to 87 riyals.
Two cement companies, Arab Cement and Eastern Cement, were also among the losers, shedding 1.2 percent and 0.3 percent respectively to 163 riyals and 374 riyals.
